transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here today because I've been feeling incredibly depressed, sad, and empty inside for a really long time now. It has been going on constantly for about a year and a month. I just can't seem to shake this heavy feeling.
During this past year, have there been any periods of at least two weeks where your symptoms were significantly more severe, or has your mood remained at this same baseline level the entire time?

My mood has stayed pretty much at the same low baseline level the entire time. It has just felt consistently bad and heavy throughout the whole year. There haven't really been any distinct periods where things suddenly got much worse than they already are.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a constant, low-level depressed mood lasting for over a year (13 months) without distinct periods of symptom exacerbation or remission, which is the hallmark clinical presentation of Persistent Depressive Disorder. Major Depressive Disorder is less likely given the absence of discrete, severe episodes.

Further assessment is needed to determine the severity, specific symptom count, and whether there have been any periods of remission or hypomania/mania.
